agent.sense: The AI acting on the user's behalf, as named in first-person transparency copy and the operation log's initiator column.

app.sense: An application in general: another app on the Mac, a cloud provider's sync app, or Cmdr itself as "the app".

click.sense: Pressing a button, link, or row with a single click ("Click to…").

coming-soon.sense: A label on a feature that isn't available yet.

example.sense: A prefix introducing a sample value in a placeholder or hint.
example.note: Many languages split the full word ("Example:") from the abbreviation ("e.g.").

filter.sense: Narrowing a list or search results by a condition (search facets, the recent-queries filter).

forget.sense: Removing a saved server, a trusted host key, a drive's index, or Ask Cmdr's notes, so Cmdr no longer remembers it.

hard-link.sense: A file-system entry sharing its data with another name (counted once on disk).

importance.sense: Cmdr's ranking of how much a folder matters to this user (image-index scope, the folder-importance tool).

on-disk-size.sense: A file's or folder's physical size on the drive (allocated blocks), as opposed to its content size.

pattern.sense: A match or rename pattern (glob, regex, or a rename template).

recent.sense: Recently used paths, searches, or selections, and the most recent download.

regex.sense: A regular expression as a search or selection mode.

repository.sense: A git repository (the .git portal, Cmdr's GitHub repository).

reset.sense: Putting a setting or shortcut back to its default value.

status.sense: A state label or column (a server's status, a license's status, an index badge's state).

subscription.sense: A paid commercial license that renews yearly.

technical-details.sense: The disclosure section in an error panel or dialog holding the raw system code and message.

theme.sense: The light, dark, or follow-the-system appearance of the app.

wildcard.sense: A placeholder character (*, ?) in a glob pattern.

worktree.sense: A git worktree (a linked checkout, kept verbatim as a git term) or the working tree of a repository.
worktree.note: The git term "worktree" is not translated; "working tree" (the checked-out files in general) may be.
